practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is the most unique and defining characteristic of Mature Harappan town planning?
practiceQuestions.sol: The gridiron layout, where streets and lanes intersect at right angles dividing the town into rectangular blocks, is the most defining characteristic.

practiceQuestions.q: The standard dimension ratio of Mature Harappan baked bricks is:
practiceQuestions.sol: A uniform ratio of 1:2:4 (typically 7x14x28 cm for houses and 10x20x40 cm for city walls) was maintained across all Mature Harappan sites.

practiceQuestions.q: In which city was the famous 'Great Bath' excavated?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Great Bath, a monumental public water tank, was excavated on the Citadel mound at Mohenjo-daro.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Harappan site has yielded a massive stone-cut water reservoir system for rainwater harvesting?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dholavira, located in the arid region of Kutch, featured a highly sophisticated system of rock-cut water reservoirs fed by dams.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the typical division of a Mature Harappan city layout?
opts: Two parts: Citadel in the west and Lower Town in the east
Three parts: Citadel, Middle Town, and Lower Town at all sites
A series of scattered villages with no center
practiceQuestions.sol: Most Harappan towns were divided into a fortified Citadel on the elevated west (ruling/religious activities) and a Lower Town on the east (common citizens).

practiceQuestions.q: The dockyard made of baked bricks was discovered at which of the following Harappan sites?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lothal in Gujarat features a massive trapezoidal basin of baked bricks identified as a tidal dockyard for maritime trade.

practiceQuestions.q: Why were ground floor walls of Harappan houses built without windows facing the main streets?
opts: To protect houses from river floods
To ensure privacy and security for the inhabitants
Because they did not know how to make window frames
To keep out the smell of the street drains
practiceQuestions.sol: Harappans prioritized privacy; ground floors had blank outer walls, and entrances were offset so passersby could not look directly inside.

practiceQuestions.q: The underground drains of Harappan streets were constructed using bricks laid in mortar made of which materials?
practiceQuestions.sol: Drains were built using fired bricks bound with a watertight mortar of gypsum, lime, and fine sand.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following statements about the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro is INCORRECT?
opts: It had steps leading down into the tank from two sides.
It was surrounded by changing rooms and galleries.
It was used primarily as a royal swimming pool for leisure.
It was made watertight using a backing of natural bitumen.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Great Bath was likely used for ritual purification bathing during public festivals, rather than as a private leisure swimming pool.

practiceQuestions.q: The masonry method where headers and stretchers alternate in successive courses to strengthen brick walls is called:
practiceQuestions.sol: The English bond masonry technique was widely used, providing excellent structural integrity, which helped walls withstand seismic activity.

practiceQuestions.q: At which site have archaeologists discovered the remains of circular brick platforms used for threshing grain?
practiceQuestions.sol: At Harappa, 18 circular brick platforms were discovered near the barracks, containing burnt traces of wheat and barley, indicating their use for grain threshing.

practiceQuestions.q: The street drainage system of Indus cities was connected to houses through:
opts: Open gutters running through front doors
Brick sumps or soakage pits where solid waste settled first
Lead pipes discharging directly into local rivers
There was no connection; house waste was thrown on roofs
practiceQuestions.sol: House waste ran into street drains through small wall apertures via intermediate brick sumps/soak pits that filtered solid waste.

practiceQuestions.q: Which site shows a unique triple-division town plan instead of the standard dual plan?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dholavira is uniquely divided into three fortified zones: the Citadel (Castle and Bailey), the Middle Town, and the Lower Town.

practiceQuestions.q: In which Indian state is the site of Banawali located, known for a lack of systematic grid planning and radial streets?
practiceQuestions.sol: Banawali is in Fatehabad district, Haryana. It is unusual because its street layout is somewhat radial and lacks a strict grid.

practiceQuestions.q: The Citadel of Harappan cities was elevated above the surrounding ground by building it on:
practiceQuestions.sol: The Citadel was constructed on huge, laboriously built mud-brick platforms (up to 6 meters high) to raise it above flood levels.

practiceQuestions.q: The main streets of Mature Harappan cities were wide enough to allow which of the following?
opts: Two wheeled bullock carts to pass each other
Nothing; streets were blocked by houses
practiceQuestions.sol: The main avenues (up to 10 meters wide) were planned to allow two bullock carts to pass each other comfortably, facilitating trade.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following materials was NOT used in the construction of Harappan residential buildings?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Harappan civilization was a Bronze Age culture and had no knowledge of iron metallurgy or structural iron.

practiceQuestions.q: The site of Lothal in Gujarat is located on the bank of which tributary of the Sabarmati River?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lothal is situated on the banks of the Bhogavo River, a key tributary of Sabarmati, giving it access to the Gulf of Khambhat.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Great Granary' at Mohenjo-daro was characterized by having a brick foundation with air flues. Why were these flues built?
opts: To allow soldiers to crawl under the building for defense
To circulate air under the wooden superstructure to keep the grain dry and prevent rot
To heat the building during winters
practiceQuestions.sol: Under-floor air flues allowed fresh air to circulate beneath the wooden granary deck, preventing dampness and rot of stored grains.

practiceQuestions.q: At which site have archaeologists found an offset wall showing independent fortifications enclosing BOTH the Citadel and Lower Town?
practiceQuestions.sol: Kalibangan in Rajasthan shows separate fortifications around both its western Citadel and eastern Lower Town.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Harappan site has yielded NO evidence of a fortified Citadel structure?
practiceQuestions.sol: Chanhudaro in Sindh is unique among Mature Harappan cities as it lacks a fortified Citadel division; it was primarily an unfortified craft-center.

practiceQuestions.q: To cover the street drains, Harappan engineers used removable slabs of which materials?
practiceQuestions.sol: Street drains were covered with large fired bricks or limestone slabs that could be removed easily by municipal cleaners.

practiceQuestions.q: The standard domestic house plan in Mature Harappan towns centered around which feature?
practiceQuestions.sol: Houses were built with rooms arranged around an open central courtyard, which was the focus of domestic life (cooking, weaving).

practiceQuestions.q: At Mohenjo-daro, how many wells are estimated to have existed to supply the city's population with water?
opts: None; they used river water directly
practiceQuestions.sol: Mohenjo-daro featured over 700 circular, brick-lined wells, averaging one well for every few households, showing excellent municipal water planning.

practiceQuestions.q: Which architectural feature indicates that Harappan houses had multiple storeys?
opts: Remains of brick staircases and sockets for wooden floor beams
practiceQuestions.sol: Staircases made of brick and rows of sockets in walls to hold thick wooden joists prove that houses had upper storeys.

practiceQuestions.q: Which city is famous for its sophisticated 'water-gate' or sluice gate mechanism to control water levels in its dockyard?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lothal's dockyard had a sluice gate made of wood/stone to lock water inside the basin during low tide so ships remained afloat.

practiceQuestions.q: The outer walls of houses facing the public street were generally:
opts: Plain, undecorated, and made of plain clay plaster over brick
Made of wood to reduce weight
practiceQuestions.sol: Harappan residential architecture was highly functional; outer walls facing streets were plain, covered with simple mud or lime plaster.

practiceQuestions.q: In which Harappan site have stone pillars and dressed stone blocks been used extensively for monumental wall foundations?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dholavira features extensive use of locally quarried dressed stone for fortification walls, pillars, and reservoirs, unlike the brick-dominant Indus plains.

practiceQuestions.q: The air flues in the granary podiums are an example of Harappan engineering addressing which problem?
practiceQuestions.sol: By circulating air under the storage decks, the flues prevented the accumulation of moisture, which would otherwise rot grain.

practiceQuestions.q: To prevent street drains from clogging, municipal authorities constructed:
opts: Large settlement sumps at street junctions to catch silt
Iron mesh grids at drain mouths
They did not prevent it; drains were left clogged
practiceQuestions.sol: Large brick sumps with removable covers were built at street junctions, letting mud settle so it could be cleared periodically.

practiceQuestions.q: Which site features a Citadel and Lower Town that are NOT separated by a wall, but share a single continuous fortified perimeter?
practiceQuestions.sol: Lothal's Citadel was not separated from the Lower Town by an internal wall; instead, the entire settlement shared a single defensive wall.

practiceQuestions.q: The L-shaped bricks found in Harappan excavations were specifically engineered for:
opts: Forming strong, interlocking corners of house walls
practiceQuestions.sol: L-shaped corner bricks allowed masons to bind intersecting walls securely without leaving weak joints.

practiceQuestions.q: The massive municipal investments in public wells, toilets, and covered drains show that Harappan rulers prioritized:
practiceQuestions.sol: The focus on drainage and clean water reflects a society that prioritized hygiene and public welfare over monumental displays of royal power.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is true regarding the drainage outlets of Harappan bathrooms?
opts: They sloped towards a wall hole that emptied directly into street drains.
They were connected to septic tanks under courtyards.
There were no drains; water was swept out of front doors.
practiceQuestions.sol: Bathroom floors sloped to a corner drain hole, from which wastewater ran through house walls into street drainage.

practiceQuestions.q: Fired or baked clay drainpipes were particularly used inside house walls to:
opts: Carry wastewater down from upper-storey toilets and baths
Serve as chimneys for kitchen smoke
practiceQuestions.sol: Clay pipes, often tapered to increase flow speed, were built vertically inside walls to guide waste from upper storeys down to street level.

practiceQuestions.q: Which Harappan city is located near the Rann of Kutch, isolated on the island of Khadir Bet?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dholavira is located on Khadir Bet island in the Great Rann of Kutch, Gujarat, surrounded by salt flats.

practiceQuestions.q: The stone dams discovered near Dholavira were built across local seasonal streams to:
opts: Divert rainwater runoff into the city's massive reservoir system
Serve as bridge crossings for traders
practiceQuestions.sol: Dams built across the Mansar and Manhar seasonal streams diverted rainwater into reservoirs surrounding the city.

practiceQuestions.q: What type of mortar was used to build the watertight brick wall of the Lothal dockyard?
practiceQuestions.sol: To hold the heavy basin walls against water pressure, builders used fired bricks joined with durable gypsum-lime mortar.

practiceQuestions.q: The absence of large defensive structures like towers with arrow-ports suggests that Harappan fortifications were designed mainly to protect against:
opts: Seasonal river floods and local bandits or cattle-raiders
practiceQuestions.sol: Fortifications served a dual purpose: acting as flood dykes against rising rivers and offering security against local bandits and animal raiders.

practiceQuestions.q: Which site has yielded circular brick kilns situated inside residential quarters, showing craft zones within the city?
practiceQuestions.sol: Mohenjo-daro's residential sectors (like DK Area) contained pottery kilns, showing that industrial work coexisted within municipal sectors.

practiceQuestions.q: The brick-paved bathroom floors of Harappan houses were sealed against leaks by using:
opts: Perfect tight-fitting joints and finely rubbed brick edges
practiceQuestions.sol: Bathroom floor bricks were carefully ground so their edges fit together perfectly, reducing gaps to prevent seepage into the subsoil.

practiceQuestions.q: Standard Mature Harappan street layouts followed a grid system. What name is given to this gridiron planning?
practiceQuestions.sol: The planning is called Chessboard or Gridiron planning due to the neat square blocks formed by intersecting streets.

practiceQuestions.q: At Dholavira, water reservoirs were carved out of which material?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dholavira's reservoirs were cut directly into the natural rock (bedrock), making them highly durable.

practiceQuestions.q: The 'Bailey' and the 'Castle' are architectural sub-divisions of the Citadel at which site?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dholavira's elevated Citadel is split into two fortified sectors: the Castle (ruling elite) and the Bailey (administrative area).

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is true regarding Harappan street sweepers or municipal maintenance?
opts: Drains were never cleaned and filled up with mud.
Removable drain covers and settlement sumps show regular cleaning took place.
practiceQuestions.sol: The existence of sumps, grit chambers, and removable covers proves that a municipal workforce regularly cleaned the drains.

practiceQuestions.q: In Harappan domestic architecture, the entrance door of a house opened into:
opts: A side lane, rather than the main street directly
practiceQuestions.sol: To ensure privacy and avoid noise/dust, doors opened into narrow side lanes instead of the busy main roads.

practiceQuestions.q: The large pillared hall excavated at Mohenjo-daro is believed to have been used as a:
opts: Assembly hall, administrative office, or marketplace
practiceQuestions.sol: The 20-pillared hall at Mohenjo-daro is interpreted as a civic assembly hall, market, or administrative council center.

practiceQuestions.q: Which site shows a transition from early mud-brick fortifications to mature fired-brick city walls?
practiceQuestions.sol: Harappa features mud-brick walls in early phases that were reinforced or replaced by massive fired-brick walls in the Mature phase.

practiceQuestions.q: The uniform municipal administration suggested by Harappan town planning collapsed during which phase?
practiceQuestions.sol: During the Late Harappan phase, municipal systems decayed, leading to narrow streets blocked by houses and broken drains.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following is the primary source of water for the reservoirs of Dholavira?
practiceQuestions.sol: Dholavira relied entirely on rainwater harvesting, collecting runoff from seasonal streams (Mansar/Manhar) during monsoons.
